data.title: Ros Chaad Thai Hosts ‘Banana Party’ to Celebrate Thai Banana Diversity
data.description: Bangkok, 23 September 2026 — Ros Chaad Thai (www.roschaadthai.com), a digital knowledge platform dedicated to Thai food and food culture by Chef Cares Foundation, invites everyone to discover the remarkable diversity of Thailand’s native bananas at “ROS CHAAD THAI BANANA PARTY” taking place on Saturday, 17 October 2026, from 10.00 to 18.00 hrs. at Bangkok Kunsthalle, Maitri Chit Road, Hua Lamphong, Bangkok.

data.title: Thai farmers, fishermen challenge IMF, World Bank at Bangkok rally
data.description: BANGKOK (THAILAND) - Thai farmers, fishermen and workers marched through Bangkok Friday as global finance and business leaders gathered for IMF and World Bank meetings, demanding a say in policies shaping their livelihoods.

data.title: SYMPHONY and Huawei Sign MOU
data.description: SYMPHONY Communication Public Company Limited and Huawei Technologies (Thailand) Co., Ltd. signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish a framework for strategic and technical cooperation. The agreement covers six areas of collaboration including intelligent network evolution, optical transport network development, virtualization platform and storage infrastructure, AI infrastructure innovation, intelligent operations and maintenance (O&M) services, and joint talent development — laying the groundwork for SYMPHONY to strengthen its network capabilities and accelerate its digital transformation journey.

data.title: Why India's voter revision drive has stoked fear and anger
data.description: NEW DELHI (INDIA) - India's sweeping overhaul of electoral rolls has triggered a political firestorm, with opposition parties accusing the Election Commission of putting millions at risk of disenfranchisement.

data.title: Families of children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
data.description: PESHAWAR (PAKISTAN) - The families of children killed in a roof collapse at a school in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, a day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.

data.title: In Malaysia, frustration grows over Indonesia haze
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Closed schools, shuttered sports centres and mass mask handouts. Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia.

data.title: Thailand ready to power RE100 companies toward 100% renewable electricity goals
data.description: On October 5, 2026, the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT), the Metropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA), the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA), and the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) discussed Thailand's renewable energy trading options in an exclusive meeting titled "Powering Corporate Ambition in Thailand's Energy Landscape." The event was held for companies committed to 100% renewable electricity targets, operating under the Climate Group, at Hyatt Regency Bangkok Sukhumvit Hotel.

data.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, Fed boss upbeat on AI
data.description: HONG KONG - Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day's tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, which Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said offered huge benefits to the global economy.

data.title: Protesters blocked from reaching IMF, World Bank meeting venue
data.description: Demonstrators faced a police blockade banning them on Friday from marching to the meeting venue of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to air grievances against the two institutions.

data.title: Tuk-tuk driver fined 1,500 baht over 4,000-baht fare demand from Russian tourists
data.description: Police have fined a tuk-tuk driver 1,500 baht after he demanded 4,000 baht from two Russian tourists, who attended The Weeknd: After Hours Til Dawn Tour for a journey to Sukhumvit 4, although they ultimately paid him only 400 baht.

data.title: Trump's new press secretary says China lacked 'proper' toilets
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked "proper toilets" in an interview that aired on Thursday.

data.title: India closes down New Delhi park ahead of 'cockroach' movement rally
data.description: NEW DELHI (INDIA) - Authorities closed a central New Delhi park Friday before a fresh protest seeking the removal of India's election chief over a voter-roll revision that critics say has disenfranchised millions.

data.title: Fresh rain brings wildlife back to Dong Yai sanctuary
data.description: BURI RAM - Dozens of wild elephants and more than 100 gaurs have been spotted feeding in Dong Yai Wildlife Sanctuary after recent rainfall replenished water sources and revived vegetation following a dry spell, officials said.

data.title: Breaking the Cycle: How Treating Mental Health and Addiction Together Leads to Lasting Healing
data.description: For a long time, society viewed substance addiction simply as a lack of willpower or a bad habit. Today, modern clinical research tells a very different story.

data.title: Five security volunteers injured in pipe bomb attack in Yala
data.description: Two homemade pipe bombs were thrown into a security unit’s operational base in Bannang Sata district, Yala province late on Thursday evening, leaving five security volunteers injured.

data.title: 'Let us build': World Bank chief outlines jobs-led development agenda
data.description: BANGKOK (THAILAND) - World Bank President Ajay Banga laid out a vision on Friday for how his multilateral development giant should operate, focusing primarily on creating jobs, expanding economic opportunity and connecting private capital to developing nations that need investment.

data.title: Fed's Warsh surprised by world economy's 'resilience'
data.description: BANGKOK (THAILAND) - US Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said on Friday, the global economy had shown unexpected resilience against strong economic shocks, as central banks battle surging inflation, while rich countries tackle spiking bond yields.

data.title: Thailand showcases sword fighting, war drums and Thai Fight at 2026 IMF–World Bank meetings
data.description: Sword displays, traditional drums and Thai Fight bouts introduce global finance delegates in Bangkok to Thailand’s martial arts and cultural traditions

data.title: Thai fruit inspires dance at IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok on October 14
data.description: The Land of Prosperity mixes Thai dance and music with fresh fruit shared with IMF–World Bank delegates in Bangkok to showcase local culture

data.title: Four killed in Indonesia battling fires causing toxic haze
data.description: JAKARTA (INDONESIA) - Four people died on Indonesia's Java island fighting the blazes that have been sending toxic smoke across southeast Asia, closing schools and fuelling a surge of respiratory complaints in the region, authorities said on Friday.

data.title: Lumphini’s lizards star in winning urban wildlife photo at Wildlife Photographer of the Year
data.description: A photograph of monitor lizards in Bangkok’s Lumphini Park by UK photographer Seth Forestson has won the Urban Wildlife category of Wildlife Photographer of the Year, an annual competition run by the Natural History Museum in London.

data.title: New airport baggage inspection starts on Friday
data.description: Airport authorities can open checked baggage during the screening process without the presence of the passenger from Friday in a new regulation to increase aviation safety.

data.title: EC urged to look at  Suchada donations
data.description: Former Democrat MP Sirichok Sopha has urged the Election Commission (EC) to investigate donations to the ruling Bhumjaithai (BJT) Party from MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap, whose Australian husband is under scrutiny for his business interests.

data.title: Revived panel to boost trade, ties after 20 years
data.description: Thailand and Egypt have agreed to expand trade and investment and strengthen ties after reviving their Joint Commission on Bilateral Cooperation following a 20-year hiatus.

data.title: Dechapol, Supissara out of Denmark Open
data.description: Mixed doubles players Dechapol Puavaranukroh and Supissara Paewsampran bowed out in the last 16 of the US$950,000 BWF Denmark Open on Thursday.

data.title: PEA grilling on EEC solar farm looms
data.description: The House committee on energy will summon the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) and private companies to clarify complaints over the selection process for a 23-billion-baht solar farm project in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC).

data.title: Cambodia dispute returns to The Hague
data.description: The second round of conciliation proceedings between Thailand and Cambodia under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Unclos) began in The Hague on Wednesday.

data.title: Amnesty expresses concerns over police conduct against IMF protesters
data.description: Amnesty International Thailand raised concerns over police conduct after observing the use of physical force against protesters, who gathered near the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group Annual Meetings on Thursday morning.

data.title: MRT Queen Sirikit National Convention Center station closed until 4pm
data.description: MRT's Blue Line station, Queen Sirikit National Convention Center will remain closed until 4pm on Friday for security reasons as it directly connects with the venue of the ongoing annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank.

data.title: PM Anutin promotes Thailand as global connector in AI era at IMF–World Bank opening on October 16
data.description: Anutin urges global partners in Bangkok to connect markets, capital and technology to support business growth, skills development and better lives.

data.title: Traffic restrictions announced around Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre on Oct 16
data.description: The Metropolitan Police Bureau has announced road closures and traffic restrictions around the Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre in Bangkok on Friday, Oct 16, to facilitate travel and ensure public safety.

data.title: Le Pen looms large as Macron enters final months on EU stage
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - The spectre of far-right leader Marine Le Pen winning France's presidency with a pledge to go head-to-head with the European Union is already giving Brussels the jitters -- and looming large over Emmanuel Macron's final months in power.

data.title: 'Mixed feelings': AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
data.description: TOKYO - Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years -- until AI cracked it in a matter of hours.

data.title: Man Utd teetering towards crisis as Man City cloud hangs over Premier League
data.description: MANCHESTER - Manchester United travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday with pressure mounting on manager Michael Carrick, while Manchester City aim to extend their perfect Premier League start despite the uncertainty over their future.

data.title: 'Multiple victims' in Oregon elementary school shooting
data.description: LOS ANGELES - A shooting at an elementary school in the northwestern state of Oregon on Thursday left "multiple victims," police said, with several media outlets reporting three children and one adult had been killed.
